subject: Microburst reconciliation and proposed netting/credit plan
messages:
From: Anita Rao <anita@quantflow.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: billing@quantflow.ai
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected microburst on 2026-10-02 — asking for reconciliation and netting

Hi Ben,

We noticed an unusual spike in our October 2nd billing (roughly 18x our baseline for a 30-minute window). The attached CSV has a sample of our requestIDs and timestamps from our side. We believe these were replayed requests from a downstream replayer and should be covered by the standard replay/netting policy you mentioned during procurement.

Quick asks:
- Can you confirm whether Redwood sees matching requestIDs/telemetry for the same window?
- If this is classified as a replay or ingestion duplication on Redwood’s side, what credit path do you propose?
- We need an ETA for resolution because our finance team is holding the payment until this is reconciled.

Appreciate a quick acknowledgement and next steps.

Best,
Anita Rao
Head of Platform, QuantFlow
Anita@quantflow.ai

Attachment: quantflow-microburst-sample-logs.csv (3 rows sample)
From: ben_carter@redwood.com <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Anita Rao <anita@quantflow.ai>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected microburst on 2026-10-02 — asking for reconciliation and netting

Hi Anita — thanks for flagging and for the CSV. Acknowledged.

Looping in Jordan (billing) and Marissa (finance ops) to pull the meter-level traces and propose a netting/credit approach. Grace I’m copying as the AM for escalation if we need a fast exception.

Plan: Jordan will surface a preliminary metering breakdown within 48 hours. If we confirm this is a replay/duplicate ingestion event, we typically apply a corrective credit for the impacted token window and, where applicable, net off the overage against next month’s invoice to avoid delaying payment. We’ll include the accounting note we use for VAT-friendly credits.

I’ll keep you updated.

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
From: jordan_blake@redwood.com <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, Anita Rao <anita@quantflow.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 10 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected microburst on 2026-10-02 — asking for reconciliation and netting

Hi Anita / team — preliminary check done. High-level notes:

- We see a 27-minute window starting 2026-10-02T14:42:00Z with a burst of ~2.1M tokens versus a 7-day baseline of ~120k tokens for the same window.
- 72% of the requests in that window share identical requestIDs or duplicate client IP + payload fingerprints. That strongly suggests replay/duplicate submission.
- Attached is a short XLSX with the per-prefix token counts we observed and the candidate set of requestIDs that correlate with your CSV. (redwood-prelim-metering-breakdown.xlsx)

Required from QuantFlow to finalize classification:
- Full replay logs (more than the 3-row sample) or the list of requestIDs for the 14:30–15:00Z window.
- Confirmation whether any batch replays were triggered by your ingest pipeline during that timeframe.

If you provide the logs, our ops team can run a deterministic matching job and produce a definitive duplicate classification. If confirmed, our standard remediation options are:
A) One-time credit for the exact overage amount (invoice reduction).
B) Netting the credit against next invoice + a credit memo (preferred for quicker cash flow for you).

Tax/VAT note: Marissa — if we credit the October invoice versus issuing a separate memo, we need to ensure the VAT reversal follows QuantFlow’s jurisdictional requirements (they’re US-based, but invoices cross-charge EU subsidiaries). I’ll leave the final wording to finance.

Next steps: QuantFlow to share full requestID list; we’ll run matching and get back with a proposed dollar credit and the accounting path. Target ETA: 48 business hours after we receive the logs.

– Jordan
Billing Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-prelim-metering-breakdown.xlsx
From: Anita Rao <anita@quantflow.ai>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: billing@quantflow.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected microburst on 2026-10-02 — asking for reconciliation and netting

Jordan — thanks for the quick look and the breakdown. Attached is a fuller export of our requestIDs for 2026-10-02T14:30:00Z–15:00:00Z (10k rows). We triggered a backfill job that mistakenly replayed a subset of requests; that was operator error on our side.

Given that, our preference is option B (net the credit against next invoice) since we’re trying to keep collections moving and avoid a separate refund workflow. Please treat this as an admission that some traffic originated from our replay job. We still want to understand whether any duplicate caused additional upstream amplification inside Redwood’s ingest layer — if the netting amount looks larger than our sample implies we’ll need the request-level match to reconcile.

Attaching: quantflow-microburst-full-20261002.csv (10k rows)

Thanks,
Anita

Attachment: quantflow-microburst-full-20261002.csv
From: ben_carter@redwood.com <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Anita Rao <anita@quantflow.ai>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 16:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected microburst on 2026-10-02 — asking for reconciliation and netting

Hi Anita — really helpful, and thanks for the transparency. We ran the deterministic match against your 10k requestIDs and here’s what we’re proposing: 

Summary of findings (final):
- Matched duplicates: 9,740 requestIDs matched Redwood ingestion records in the burst window.
- Net over-count (tokens attributable to duplicates): 1,936,400 tokens.
- Dollar value at QuantFlow’s current tier: $1,456.80.

Proposed remediation (to keep collections moving):
1) Issue a credit memo for $1,456.80 that will be netted against QuantFlow’s November invoice (option B). We will label the memo with your PO reference and include an accounting note for VAT reversal if needed.
2) Marissa will prepare the credit memo and a short accounting note that documents the duplicate origin and treatment for your finance team.
3) If you need the credit expressed as a separate refund instead, we can do that but it will delay netting by ~5–7 business days while payments operations issues a refund.

Marissa, can you confirm the credit memo ID and whether we should include a VAT reversal line for QuantFlow’s EU subsidiary (they mentioned cross-entity billing in their PO)?

Anita — if that plan works, I’ll mark this thread resolved and update the HubSpot record (DOC-8872).

Thanks all — and apologize for the disruption. Also recommending a brief runbook share between our ops teams to reduce replay amplification risk going forward.

Best,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
